Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Stellix is keen to move forward but procurement has a few redline asks on the Order Form before we can route the PO. Attached is our annotated draft (Stellix_OrderForm_Redline_20270405.pdf). High-level items they flagged: 

- Net terms: procurement prefers Net45 (our standard is Net30). Please confirm if you can accept Net45 and whether early-pay discounts are available.
- Minimum commit proration: they want the minimum commit to be prorated across the first 30 days if the service start is delayed.
- Invoicing remit: they need the invoice remitted to Stellix Sweden AB (local EU entity). Can you confirm Redwood's invoicing entity and whether you can send entity-level invoices?
- Taxes / withholding: for EU customers they ask whether Redwood will gross-up or if Stellix should withhold taxes locally (France/Sweden scenarios). We need language that clears responsibility for withholding taxes and VAT evidence.

Can someone from legal/finance at Redwood propose the exact clause language so we can pass to our legal for quick sign-off? If it helps, happy to set a short call this week.

Thanks,
Anna

Anna — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Looping in Karthik from Legal and Ben from Sales to propose a workable path.

Quick summary of Redwood's current position / suggested compromises:
- Net terms: we can agree to Net45 on this deal but will include a 1.5% early-pay discount if paid within 15 days.
- Minimum commit proration: we can accept prorated commitment for delayed starts up to 45 days, beyond that we'll need an amended schedule. We'll propose explicit proration math in the OF.
- Invoicing remit / entity: Redwood invoices are normally issued by Redwood Inference, Inc. (US entity). For EU customers we can issue a local-entity invoice through our EU subsidiary (Redwood Inference EU AB) if customer requires. Need Stellix legal to confirm remit-to entity and VAT registration number to put on the invoice.
- Taxes / withholding: our preference is that customer handles local withholding and provides evidence; Redwood will provide a gross-up only in limited circumstances and with prior approval. We recommend a clause that: (a) identifies which party is responsible for withholding, (b) requires customer to provide timely documentation (tax receipts/evidence), and (c) allows Redwood to issue an invoice for any shortfall if withholding reduces net amounts. Karthik — suggested language below?

Next steps: Ben / I can update the OF with the proration table and invoice recipient fields; Karthik to provide legal clause. Can we aim to get a revised OF and a short call on Wed 4/7 to resolve?

Cheers,

All — drafted some concise redline language below that should address Stellix's procurement asks while protecting Redwood's revenue and tax exposure. Please review and let me know if you want any adjustments before we put it into the OF draft.

Proposed clauses (to insert in Order Form / Billing section):
1) Invoicing and Remit-To: Redwood Inference, Inc. (or Redwood Inference EU AB where requested by Customer) will issue invoices showing the legal entity and VAT/Tax ID requested by the Customer. Customer shall provide written remit-to instructions and any local tax IDs necessary for compliant invoicing no later than ten (10) days following Effective Date.

2) Taxes and Withholding: Unless otherwise agreed in writing, Customer is responsible for any applicable taxes, duties, and similar charges, including any withholding taxes imposed by Customer's jurisdiction. If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold any Taxes from payments to Redwood, Customer shall (a) notify Redwood in writing prior to withholding; (b) withhold only the minimum required by law; and (c) promptly provide Redwood with official documentation evidencing the amount and payment of such withholding to the relevant tax authority. If withholding reduces the net amount received by Redwood, Customer shall either (i) increase the payment to Gross-Up the amount so that Redwood receives the full invoiced amount, or (ii) where Gross-Up is not permitted or feasible, Customer shall provide proof of payment to the tax authority and Redwood may seek recovery of the shortfall in accordance with the dispute resolution process.

3) Minimum Commit Proration: If the Service Start Date is delayed at Customer's request or due to Customer-provided dependencies, the Minimum Commitment for the initial billing period shall be prorated on a pro-rata daily basis for delays up to forty-five (45) days. Delays exceeding forty-five (45) days will require an amendment to the Order Form reflecting either an adjusted Minimum Commitment or revised payment schedule.

4) Net Terms and Early Payment: Standard payment terms for this Order Form will be Net30. For this transaction only, Redwood agrees to Net45 in exchange for a 1.5% early-payment discount if the invoice is paid within fifteen (15) calendar days. All other billing terms remain unchanged.

I have kept the language intentionally prescriptive to avoid back-and-forth on interpretation. If Stellix confirms remit-to entity (Sweden AB) and agrees to the documentation timing, I can include the exact text in the attached Word OF (RW-OF-updates-draft-20270407.docx).
